verses.first: For they did not take the land by their sword, nor did their arm win the victory for them;
verses.second: but your right hand, your arm, and the light of your countenance, because you favored them.

verses.first: You are my King and my God;
verses.second: you command victories for Jacob.

verses.first: Through you we pushed back our adversaries;
verses.second: through your Name we trampled on those who rose up against us.

verses.first: For I do not rely on my bow,
verses.second: and my sword does not give me the victory.

verses.first: Surely, you gave us victory over our adversaries
verses.second: and put those who hate us to shame.

verses.first: Every day we gloried in God,
verses.second: and we will praise your Name for ever.

verses.first: Nevertheless, you have rejected and humbled us
verses.second: and do not go forth with our armies.

verses.first: You have made us fall back before our adversary,
verses.second: and our enemies have plundered us.

verses.first: You have made us like sheep to be eaten
verses.second: and have scattered us among the nations.

verses.first: You are selling your people for a trifle
verses.second: and are making no profit on the sale of them.

verses.first: You have made us the scorn of our neighbors,
verses.second: a mockery and derision to those around us.

verses.first: You have made us a byword among the nations,
verses.second: a laughing-stock among the peoples.

verses.first: My humiliation is daily before me,
verses.second: and shame has covered my face;

verses.first: Because of the taunts of the mockers and blasphemers,
verses.second: because of the enemy and avenger.

verses.first: All this has come upon us;
verses.second: yet we have not forgotten you, nor have we betrayed your covenant.

verses.first: Our heart never turned back,
verses.second: nor did our footsteps stray from your path;

verses.first: Though you thrust us down into a place of misery,
verses.second: and covered us over with deep darkness.

verses.first: If we have forgotten the Name of our God,
verses.second: or stretched out our hands to some strange god,

verses.first: Will not God find it out?
verses.second: for he knows the secrets of the heart.

verses.first: Indeed, for your sake we are killed all the day long;
verses.second: we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.

verses.first: Awake, O Lord! why are you sleeping?
verses.second: Arise! do not reject us for ever.

verses.first: Why have you hidden your face
verses.second: and forgotten our affliction and oppression?

verses.first: We sink down into the dust;
verses.second: our body cleaves to the ground.

verses.first: Rise up, and help us,
verses.second: and save us, for the sake of your steadfast love.

verses.first: My heart is stirring with a noble song; let me recite what I have fashioned for the king;
verses.second: my tongue shall be the pen of a skilled writer.

verses.first: You are the fairest of men;
verses.second: grace flows from your lips, because God has blessed you for ever.

verses.first: Strap your sword upon your thigh, O mighty warrior,
verses.second: in your pride and in your majesty.

verses.first: Ride out and conquer in the cause of truth
verses.second: and for the sake of justice.

verses.first: Your right hand will show you marvelous things;
verses.second: your arrows are very sharp, O mighty warrior.

verses.first: The peoples are falling at your feet,
verses.second: and the king’s enemies are losing heart.

verses.first: Your throne, O God, endures for ever and ever,
verses.second: a scepter of righteousness is the scepter of your kingdom; you love righteousness and hate iniquity.

verses.first: Therefore God, your God, has anointed you
verses.second: with the oil of gladness above your fellows.

verses.first: All your garments are fragrant with myrrh, aloes, and cassia,
verses.second: and the music of strings from ivory palaces makes you glad.

verses.first: Kings’ daughters stand among the ladies of the court;
verses.second: on your right hand is the queen, adorned with the gold of Ophir.

verses.first: “Hear, O daughter; consider and listen closely;
verses.second: forget your people and your father’s house.

verses.first: The king will have pleasure in your beauty;
verses.second: he is your master; therefore do him honor.

verses.first: The people of Tyre are here with a gift;
verses.second: the rich among the people seek your favor.”

verses.first: All glorious is the princess as she enters;
verses.second: her gown is cloth-of-gold.

verses.first: In embroidered apparel she is brought to the king;
verses.second: after her the bridesmaids follow in procession.

verses.first: With joy and gladness they are brought,
verses.second: and enter into the palace of the king.

verses.first: “In place of fathers, O king, you shall have sons;
verses.second: you shall make them princes over all the earth.

verses.first: I will make your name to be remembered from one generation to another;
verses.second: therefore nations will praise you for ever and ever.”

verses.first: God is our refuge and strength,
verses.second: a very present help in trouble.

verses.first: Therefore we will not fear, though the earth be moved,
verses.second: and though the mountains be toppled into the depths of the sea;

verses.first: Though its waters rage and foam,
verses.second: and though the mountains tremble at its tumult.

verses.first: The Lord of hosts is with us;
verses.second: the God of Jacob is our stronghold.

verses.first: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God,
verses.second: the holy habitation of the Most High.

verses.first: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be overthrown;
verses.second: God shall help her at the break of day.

verses.first: The nations make much ado, and the kingdoms are shaken;
verses.second: God has spoken, and the earth shall melt away.

verses.first: The Lord of hosts is with us;
verses.second: the God of Jacob is our stronghold.

verses.first: Come now and look upon the works of the Lord,
verses.second: what awesome things he has done on earth.

verses.first: It is he who makes war to cease in all the world;
verses.second: he breaks the bow, and shatters the spear, and burns the shields with fire.

verses.first: “Be still, then, and know that I am God;
verses.second: I will be exalted among the nations; I will be exalted in the earth.”

verses.first: The Lord of hosts is with us;
verses.second: the God of Jacob is our stronghold.

verses.first: Clap your hands, all you peoples;
verses.second: shout to God with a cry of joy.

verses.first: For the Lord Most High is to be feared;
verses.second: he is the great King over all the earth.

verses.first: He subdues the peoples under us,
verses.second: and the nations under our feet.

verses.first: He chooses our inheritance for us,
verses.second: the pride of Jacob whom he loves.

verses.first: God has gone up with a shout,
verses.second: the Lord with the sound of the ram’s-horn.

verses.first: Sing praises to God, sing praises;
verses.second: sing praises to our King, sing praises.

verses.first: For God is King of all the earth;
verses.second: sing praises with all your skill.

verses.first: God reigns over the nations;
verses.second: God sits upon his holy throne.

verses.first: The nobles of the peoples have gathered together
verses.second: with the people of the God of Abraham.

verses.first: The rulers of the earth belong to God,
verses.second: and he is highly exalted.

verses.first: Great is the Lord, and highly to be praised;
verses.second: in the city of our God is his holy hill.

verses.first: Beautiful and lofty, the joy of all the earth, is the hill of Zion,
verses.second: the very center of the world and the city of the great King.

verses.first: God is in her citadels;
verses.second: he is known to be her sure refuge.

verses.first: Behold, the kings of the earth assembled
verses.second: and marched forward together.

verses.first: They looked and were astounded;
verses.second: they retreated and fled in terror.

verses.first: Trembling seized them there;
verses.second: they writhed like a woman in childbirth, like ships of the sea when the east wind shatters them.

verses.first: As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God;
verses.second: God has established her for ever.

verses.first: We have waited in silence on your loving-kindness, O God,
verses.second: in the midst of your temple.

verses.first: Your praise, like your Name, O God, reaches to the world’s end;
verses.second: your right hand is full of justice.

verses.first: Let Mount Zion be glad and the cities of Judah rejoice,
verses.second: because of your judgments.

verses.first: Make the circuit of Zion; walk round about her;
verses.second: count the number of her towers.

verses.first: Consider well her bulwarks; examine her strongholds;
verses.second: that you may tell those who come after.

verses.first: This God is our God for ever and ever;
verses.second: he shall be our guide for evermore.

verses.first: Hear this, all you peoples; hearken, all you who dwell in the world,
verses.second: you of high degree and low, rich and poor together.

verses.first: My mouth shall speak of wisdom,
verses.second: and my heart shall meditate on understanding.

verses.first: I will incline my ear to a proverb
verses.second: and set forth my riddle upon the harp.

verses.first: Why should I be afraid in evil days,
verses.second: when the wickedness of those at my heels surrounds me,

verses.first: The wickedness of those who put their trust in their goods,
verses.second: and boast of their great riches?

verses.first: We can never ransom ourselves,
verses.second: or deliver to God the price of our life;

verses.first: For the ransom of our life is so great,
verses.second: that we should never have enough to pay it,

verses.first: In order to live for ever and ever,
verses.second: and never see the grave.

verses.first: For we see that the wise die also; like the dull and stupid they perish
verses.second: and leave their wealth to those who come after them.

verses.first: Their graves shall be their homes for ever, their dwelling places from generation to generation,
verses.second: though they call the lands after their own names.

verses.first: Even though honored, they cannot live for ever;
verses.second: they are like the beasts that perish.

verses.first: Such is the way of those who foolishly trust in themselves,
verses.second: and the end of those who delight in their own words.

verses.first: Like a flock of sheep they are destined to die; Death is their shepherd;
verses.second: they go down straightway to the grave.

verses.first: Their form shall waste away,
verses.second: and the land of the dead shall be their home.

verses.first: But God will ransom my life;
verses.second: he will snatch me from the grasp of death.

verses.first: Do not be envious when some become rich,
verses.second: or when the grandeur of their house increases;

verses.first: For they will carry nothing away at their death,
verses.second: nor will their grandeur follow them.

verses.first: Though they thought highly of themselves while they lived,
verses.second: and were praised for their success,

verses.first: They shall join the company of their forebears,
verses.second: who will never see the light again.

verses.first: Those who are honored, but have no understanding,
verses.second: are like the beasts that perish.

verses.first: The Lord, the God of gods, has spoken;
verses.second: he has called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.

verses.first: Out of Zion, perfect in its beauty,
verses.second: God reveals himself in glory.

verses.first: Our God will come and will not keep silence;
verses.second: before him there is a consuming flame, and round about him a raging storm.

verses.first: He calls the heavens and the earth from above
verses.second: to witness the judgment of his people.

verses.first: “Gather before me my loyal followers,
verses.second: those who have made a covenant with me and sealed it with sacrifice.”

verses.first: Let the heavens declare the rightness of his cause;
verses.second: for God himself is judge.

verses.first: Hear, O my people, and I will speak: “O Israel, I will bear witness against you;
verses.second: for I am God, your God.

verses.first: I do not accuse you because of your sacrifices;
verses.second: your offerings are always before me.

verses.first: I will take no bull-calf from your stalls,
verses.second: nor he-goats out of your pens;

verses.first: For all the beasts of the forest are mine,
verses.second: the herds in their thousands upon the hills.

verses.first: I know every bird in the sky,
verses.second: and the creatures of the fields are in my sight.

verses.first: If I were hungry, I would not tell you,
verses.second: for the whole world is mine and all that is in it.

verses.first: Do you think I eat the flesh of bulls,
verses.second: or drink the blood of goats?

verses.first: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving
verses.second: and make good your vows to the Most High.

verses.first: Call upon me in the day of trouble;
verses.second: I will deliver you, and you shall honor me.”

verses.first: But to the wicked God says:
verses.second: “Why do you recite my statutes, and take my covenant upon your lips;

verses.first: Since you refuse discipline,
verses.second: and toss my words behind your back?

verses.first: When you see a thief, you make him your friend,
verses.second: and you cast in your lot with adulterers.

verses.first: You have loosed your lips for evil,
verses.second: and harnessed your tongue to a lie.

verses.first: You are always speaking evil of your brother
verses.second: and slandering your own mother’s son.

verses.first: These things you have done, and I kept still,
verses.second: and you thought that I am like you.”

verses.first: “I have made my accusation;
verses.second: I have put my case in order before your eyes.

verses.first: Consider this well, you who forget God,
verses.second: lest I rend you and there be none to deliver you.

verses.first: Whoever offers me the sacrifice of thanksgiving honors me;
verses.second: but to those who keep in my way will I show the salvation of God.”

verses.first: Have mercy on me, O God, according to your loving-kindness;
verses.second: in your great compassion blot out my offenses.

verses.first: Wash me through and through from my wickedness
verses.second: and cleanse me from my sin.

verses.first: For I know my transgressions,
verses.second: and my sin is ever before me.

verses.first: Against you only have I sinned
verses.second: and done what is evil in your sight.

verses.first: And so you are justified when you speak
verses.second: and upright in your judgment.

verses.first: Indeed, I have been wicked from my birth,
verses.second: a sinner from my mother’s womb.

verses.first: For behold, you look for truth deep within me,
verses.second: and will make me understand wisdom secretly.

verses.first: Purge me from my sin, and I shall be pure;
verses.second: wash me, and I shall be clean indeed.

verses.first: Make me hear of joy and gladness,
verses.second: that the body you have broken may rejoice.

verses.first: Hide your face from my sins
verses.second: and blot out all my iniquities.

verses.first: Create in me a clean heart, O God,
verses.second: and renew a right spirit within me.

verses.first: Cast me not away from your presence
verses.second: and take not your holy Spirit from me.

verses.first: Give me the joy of your saving help again
verses.second: and sustain me with your bountiful Spirit.

verses.first: I shall teach your ways to the wicked,
verses.second: and sinners shall return to you.

verses.first: Deliver me from death, O God,
verses.second: and my tongue shall sing of your righteousness, O God of my salvation.

verses.first: Open my lips, O Lord,
verses.second: and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.

verses.first: Had you desired it, I would have offered sacrifice,
verses.second: but you take no delight in burnt-offerings.

verses.first: The sacrifice of God is a troubled spirit;
verses.second: a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.

verses.first: Be favorable and gracious to Zion,
verses.second: and rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

verses.first: Then you will be pleased with the appointed sacrifices, with burnt-offerings and oblations;
verses.second: then shall they offer young bullocks upon your altar.

verses.first: You tyrant, why do you boast of wickedness
verses.second: against the godly all day long?

verses.first: You plot ruin; your tongue is like a sharpened razor,
verses.second: O worker of deception. `

verses.first: You love evil more than good
verses.second: and lying more than speaking the truth.

verses.first: You love all words that hurt,
verses.second: O you deceitful tongue.

verses.first: Oh, that God would demolish you utterly,
verses.second: topple you, and snatch you from your dwelling, and root you out of the land of the living!

verses.first: The righteous shall see and tremble,
verses.second: and they shall laugh at him, saying,

verses.first: “This is the one who did not take God for a refuge,
verses.second: but trusted in great wealth and relied upon wickedness.”

verses.first: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God;
verses.second: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.

verses.first: I will give you thanks for what you have done
verses.second: and declare the goodness of your Name in the presence of the godly.

verses.first: The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.”
verses.second: All are corrupt and commit abominable acts; there is none who does any good.

verses.first: God looks down from heaven upon us all,
verses.second: to see if there is any who is wise, if there is one who seeks after God.

verses.first: Every one has proved faithless; all alike have turned bad;
verses.second: there is none who does good; no, not one.

verses.first: Have they no knowledge, those evildoers
verses.second: who eat up my people like bread and do not call upon God?

verses.first: See how greatly they tremble, such trembling as never was;
verses.second: for God has scattered the bones of the enemy; they are put to shame, because God has rejected them.

verses.first: Oh, that Israel’s deliverance would come out of Zion!
verses.second: when God restores the fortunes of his people Jacob will rejoice and Israel be glad.

verses.first: Save me, O God, by your Name;
verses.second: in your might, defend my cause.

verses.first: Hear my prayer, O God;
verses.second: give ear to the words of my mouth.

verses.first: For the arrogant have risen up against me, and the ruthless have sought my life,
verses.second: those who have no regard for God.

verses.first: Behold, God is my helper;
verses.second: it is the Lord who sustains my life.

verses.first: Render evil to those who spy on me;
verses.second: in your faithfulness, destroy them.

verses.first: I will offer you a freewill sacrifice
verses.second: and praise your Name, O Lord, for it is good.

verses.first: For you have rescued me from every trouble,
verses.second: and my eye has seen the ruin of my foes.

verses.first: Hear my prayer, O God;
verses.second: do not hide yourself from my petition.

verses.first: Listen to me and answer me;
verses.second: I have no peace, because of my cares.

verses.first: I am shaken by the noise of the enemy
verses.second: and by the pressure of the wicked;

verses.first: For they have cast an evil spell upon me
verses.second: and are set against me in fury.

verses.first: My heart quakes within me,
verses.second: and the terrors of death have fallen upon me.

verses.first: Fear and trembling have come over me,
verses.second: and horror overwhelms me.

verses.first: And I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove!
verses.second: I would fly away and be at rest.

verses.first: I would flee to a far-off place
verses.second: and make my lodging in the wilderness.

verses.first: I would hasten to escape
verses.second: from the stormy wind and tempest.”

verses.first: Swallow them up, O Lord; confound their speech;
verses.second: for I have seen violence and strife in the city.

verses.first: Day and night the watchmen make their rounds upon her walls,
verses.second: but trouble and misery are in the midst of her.

verses.first: There is corruption at her heart;
verses.second: her streets are never free of oppression and deceit.

verses.first: For had it been an adversary who taunted me, then I could have borne it;
verses.second: or had it been an enemy who vaunted himself against me, then I could have hidden from him.

verses.first: But it was you, a man after my own heart,
verses.second: my companion, my own familiar friend.

verses.first: We took sweet counsel together,
verses.second: and walked with the throng in the house of God.

verses.first: Let death come upon them suddenly; let them go down alive into the grave;
verses.second: for wickedness is in their dwellings, in their very midst.

verses.first: But I will call upon God,
verses.second: and the Lord will deliver me.

verses.first: In the evening, in the morning, and at noonday, I will complain and lament,
verses.second: and he will hear my voice.

verses.first: He will bring me safely back from the battle waged against me;
verses.second: for there are many who fight me.

verses.first: God, who is enthroned of old, will hear me and bring them down;
verses.second: they never change; they do not fear God.

verses.first: My companion stretched forth his hand against his comrade;
verses.second: he has broken his covenant.

verses.first: His speech is softer than butter,
verses.second: but war is in his heart.

verses.first: His words are smoother than oil,
verses.second: but they are drawn swords.

verses.first: Cast your burden upon the Lord, and he will sustain you;
verses.second: he will never let the righteous stumble.

verses.first: For you will bring the bloodthirsty and deceitful
verses.second: down to the pit of destruction, O God.

verses.first: They shall not live out half their days,
verses.second: but I will put my trust in you.

verses.first: Have mercy on me, O God, for my enemies are hounding me;
verses.second: all day long they assault and oppress me.

verses.first: They hound me all the day long;
verses.second: truly there are many who fight against me, O Most High.

verses.first: Whenever I am afraid,
verses.second: I will put my trust in you.

verses.first: In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust and will not be afraid,
verses.second: for what can flesh do to me?

verses.first: All day long they damage my cause;
verses.second: their only thought is to do me evil.

verses.first: They band together; they lie in wait;
verses.second: they spy upon my footsteps; because they seek my life.

verses.first: Shall they escape despite their wickedness?
verses.second: O God, in your anger, cast down the peoples.

verses.first: You have noted my lamentation; put my tears into your bottle;
verses.second: are they not recorded in your book?

verses.first: Whenever I call upon you, my enemies will be put to flight;
verses.second: this I know, for God is on my side.

verses.first: In God the Lord, whose word I praise, in God I trust and will not be afraid,
verses.second: for what can mortals do to me?

verses.first: I am bound by the vow I made to you, O God;
verses.second: I will present to you thank-offerings;

verses.first: For you have rescued my soul from death and my feet from stumbling,
verses.second: that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

verses.first: Be merciful to me, O God, be merciful, for I have taken refuge in you;
verses.second: in the shadow of your wings will I take refuge until this time of trouble has gone by.

verses.first: I will call upon the Most High God,
verses.second: the God who maintains my cause.

verses.first: He will send from heaven and save me; he will confound those who trample upon me;
verses.second: God will send forth his love and his faithfulness.

verses.first: I lie in the midst of lions that devour the people;
verses.second: their teeth are spears and arrows, their tongue a sharp sword.

verses.first: They have laid a net for my feet, and I am bowed low;
verses.second: they have dug a pit before me, but have fallen into it themselves.

verses.first: Exalt yourself above the heavens, O God,
verses.second: and your glory over all the earth.

verses.first: My heart is firmly fixed, O God, my heart is fixed;
verses.second: I will sing and make melody.

verses.first: Wake up, my spirit; awake, lute and harp;
verses.second: I myself will waken the dawn.

verses.first: I will confess you among the peoples, O Lord;
verses.second: I will sing praise to you among the nations.

verses.first: For your loving-kindness is greater than the heavens,
verses.second: and your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

verses.first: Exalt yourself above the heavens, O God,
verses.second: and your glory over all the earth.

verses.first: Do you indeed decree righteousness, you rulers?
verses.second: do you judge the peoples with equity?

verses.first: No; you devise evil in your hearts,
verses.second: and your hands deal out violence in the land.

verses.first: The wicked are perverse from the womb;
verses.second: liars go astray from their birth.

verses.first: They are as venomous as a serpent,
verses.second: they are like the deaf adder which stops its ears,

verses.first: Which does not heed the voice of the charmer,
verses.second: no matter how skillful his charming.

verses.first: O God, break their teeth in their mouths;
verses.second: pull the fangs of the young lions, O Lord.

verses.first: Let them vanish like water that runs off;
verses.second: let them wither like trodden grass.

verses.first: Let them be like the snail that melts away,
verses.second: like a stillborn child that never sees the sun.

verses.first: Before they bear fruit, let them be cut down like a brier;
verses.second: like thorns and thistles let them be swept away.

verses.first: The righteous will be glad when they see the vengeance;
verses.second: they will bathe their feet in the blood of the wicked.

verses.first: And they will say, “Surely, there is a reward for the righteous;
verses.second: surely, there is a God who rules in the earth.”

verses.first: Rescue me from my enemies, O God;
verses.second: protect me from those who rise up against me.

verses.first: Rescue me from evildoers
verses.second: and save me from those who thirst for my blood.

verses.first: See how they lie in wait for my life, how the mighty gather together against me;
verses.second: not for any offense or fault of mine, O Lord.

verses.first: Not because of any guilt of mine
verses.second: they run and prepare themselves for battle.

verses.first: Rouse yourself, come to my side, and see;
verses.second: for you, Lord God of hosts, are Israel’s God.

verses.first: Awake, and punish all the ungodly;
verses.second: show no mercy to those who are faithless and evil.

verses.first: They go to and fro in the evening;
verses.second: they snarl like dogs and run about the city.

verses.first: Behold, they boast with their mouths, and taunts are on their lips;
verses.second: “For who,” they say, “will hear us?”

verses.first: But you, O Lord, you laugh at them;
verses.second: you laugh all the ungodly to scorn.

verses.first: My eyes are fixed on you, O my Strength;
verses.second: for you, O God, are my stronghold.

verses.first: My merciful God comes to meet me;
verses.second: God will let me look in triumph on my enemies.

verses.first: Slay them, O God, lest my people forget;
verses.second: send them reeling by your might and put them down, O Lord our shield.

verses.first: For the sins of their mouths, for the words of their lips, for the cursing and lies that they utter,
verses.second: let them be caught in their pride.

verses.first: Make an end of them in your wrath;
verses.second: make an end of them, and they shall be no more.

verses.first: Let everyone know that God rules in Jacob,
verses.second: and to the ends of the earth.

verses.first: They go to and fro in the evening;
verses.second: they snarl like dogs and run about the city.

verses.first: They forage for food,
verses.second: and if they are not filled, they howl.

verses.first: For my part, I will sing of your strength;
verses.second: I will celebrate your love in the morning;

verses.first: For you have become my stronghold,
verses.second: a refuge in the day of my trouble.

verses.first: To you, O my Strength, will I sing;
verses.second: for you, O God, are my stronghold and my merciful God.

verses.first: O God, you have cast us off and broken us;
verses.second: you have been angry; oh, take us back to you again.

verses.first: You have shaken the earth and split it open;
verses.second: repair the cracks in it, for it totters.

verses.first: You have made your people know hardship;
verses.second: you have given us wine that makes us stagger.

verses.first: You have set up a banner for those who fear you,
verses.second: to be a refuge from the power of the bow.

verses.first: Save us by your right hand and answer us,
verses.second: that those who are dear to you may be delivered.

verses.first: God spoke from his holy place and said:
verses.second: “I will exult and parcel out Shechem; I will divide the valley of Succoth.

verses.first: Gilead is mine and Manasseh is mine;
verses.second: Ephraim is my helmet and Judah my scepter.

verses.first: Moab is my wash-basin, on Edom I throw down my sandal to claim it,
verses.second: and over Philistia will I shout in triumph.”

verses.first: Who will lead me into the strong city?
verses.second: who will bring me into Edom?

verses.first: Have you not cast us off, O God?
verses.second: you no longer go out, O God, with our armies.

verses.first: Grant us your help against the enemy,
verses.second: for vain is the help of man.

verses.first: With God we will do valiant deeds,
verses.second: and he shall tread our enemies under foot.

verses.first: Hear my cry, O God,
verses.second: and listen to my prayer.

verses.first: I call upon you from the ends of the earth with heaviness in my heart;
verses.second: set me upon the rock that is higher than I.

verses.first: For you have been my refuge,
verses.second: a strong tower against the enemy.

verses.first: I will dwell in your house for ever;
verses.second: I will take refuge under the cover of your wings.

verses.first: For you, O God, have heard my vows;
verses.second: you have granted me the heritage of those who fear your Name.

verses.first: Add length of days to the king’s life;
verses.second: let his years extend over many generations.

verses.first: Let him sit enthroned before God for ever;
verses.second: bid love and faithfulness watch over him.

verses.first: So will I always sing the praise of your Name,
verses.second: and day by day I will fulfill my vows.

verses.first: For God alone my soul in silence waits;
verses.second: from him comes my salvation.

verses.first: He alone is my rock and my salvation,
verses.second: my stronghold, so that I shall not be greatly shaken.

verses.first: How long will you assail me to crush me, all of you together,
verses.second: as if you were a leaning fence, a toppling wall?

verses.first: They seek only to bring me down from my place of honor;
verses.second: lies are their chief delight.

verses.first: They bless with their lips,
verses.second: but in their hearts they curse.

verses.first: For God alone my soul in silence waits;
verses.second: truly, my hope is in him.

verses.first: He alone is my rock and my salvation,
verses.second: my stronghold, so that I shall not be shaken.

verses.first: In God is my safety and my honor;
verses.second: God is my strong rock and my refuge.

verses.first: Put your trust in him always, O people,
verses.second: pour out your hearts before him, for God is our refuge.

verses.first: Those of high degree are but a fleeting breath,
verses.second: even those of low estate cannot be trusted.

verses.first: On the scales they are lighter than a breath,
verses.second: all of them together.

verses.first: Put no trust in extortion; in robbery take no empty pride;
verses.second: though wealth increase, set not your heart upon it.

verses.first: God has spoken once, twice have I heard it,
verses.second: that power belongs to God.

verses.first: Steadfast love is yours, O Lord,
verses.second: for you repay everyone according to his deeds.

verses.first: O God, you are my God; eagerly I seek you;
verses.second: my soul thirsts for you, my flesh faints for you, as in a barren and dry land where there is no water.

verses.first: Therefore I have gazed upon you in your holy place,
verses.second: that I might behold your power and your glory.

verses.first: For your loving-kindness is better than life itself;
verses.second: my lips shall give you praise.

verses.first: So will I bless you as long as I live
verses.second: and lift up my hands in your Name.

verses.first: My soul is content, as with marrow and fatness,
verses.second: and my mouth praises you with joyful lips,

verses.first: When I remember you upon my bed,
verses.second: and meditate on you in the night watches.

verses.first: For you have been my helper,
verses.second: and under the shadow of your wings I will rejoice.

verses.first: My soul clings to you;
verses.second: your right hand holds me fast.

verses.first: May those who seek my life to destroy it
verses.second: go down into the depths of the earth;

verses.first: Let them fall upon the edge of the sword,
verses.second: and let them be food for jackals.

verses.first: But the king will rejoice in God; all those who swear by him will be glad;
verses.second: for the mouth of those who speak lies shall be stopped.

verses.first: Hear my voice, O God, when I complain;
verses.second: protect my life from fear of the enemy.

verses.first: Hide me from the conspiracy of the wicked,
verses.second: from the mob of evildoers.

verses.first: They sharpen their tongue like a sword,
verses.second: and aim their bitter words like arrows,

verses.first: That they may shoot down the blameless from ambush;
verses.second: they shoot without warning and are not afraid.

verses.first: They hold fast to their evil course;
verses.second: they plan how they may hide their snares.

verses.first: They say, “Who will see us? who will find out our crimes?
verses.second: we have thought out a perfect plot.”

verses.first: The human mind and heart are a mystery;
verses.second: but God will loose an arrow at them, and suddenly they will be wounded.

verses.first: He will make them trip over their tongues,
verses.second: and all who see them will shake their heads.

verses.first: Everyone will stand in awe and declare God’s deeds;
verses.second: they will recognize his works.

verses.first: The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and put their trust in him,
verses.second: and all who are true of heart will glory.

verses.first: You are to be praised, O God, in Zion;
verses.second: to you shall vows be performed in Jerusalem.

verses.first: To you that hear prayer shall all flesh come,
verses.second: because of their transgressions.

verses.first: Our sins are stronger than we are,
verses.second: but you will blot them out.

verses.first: Happy are they whom you choose and draw to your courts to dwell there!
verses.second: they will be satisfied by the beauty of your house, by the holiness of your temple.

verses.first: Awesome things will you show us in your righteousness, O God of our salvation,
verses.second: O Hope of all the ends of the earth and of the seas that are far away.

verses.first: You make fast the mountains by your power;
verses.second: they are girded about with might.

verses.first: You still the roaring of the seas,
verses.second: the roaring of their waves, and the clamor of the peoples.

verses.first: Those who dwell at the ends of the earth will tremble at your marvelous signs;
verses.second: you make the dawn and the dusk to sing for joy.

verses.first: You visit the earth and water it abundantly; you make it very plenteous;
verses.second: the river of God is full of water.

verses.first: You prepare the grain,
verses.second: for so you provide for the earth.

verses.first: I You drench the furrows and smooth out the ridges;
verses.second: with heavy rain you soften the ground and bless its increase.

verses.first: You crown the year with your goodness,
verses.second: and your paths overflow with plenty.

verses.first: May the fields of the wilderness be rich for grazing,
verses.second: and the hills be clothed with joy.

verses.first: May the meadows cover themselves with flocks, and the valleys cloak themselves with grain;
verses.second: let them shout for joy and sing.

verses.first: Be joyful in God, all you lands;
verses.second: sing the glory of his Name; sing the glory of his praise.

verses.first: Say to God, “How awesome are your deeds!
verses.second: because of your great strength your enemies cringe before you.

verses.first: All the earth bows down before you,
verses.second: sings to you, sings out your Name.”

verses.first: Come now and see the works of God,
verses.second: how wonderful he is in his doing toward all people.

verses.first: He turned the sea into dry land, so that they went through the water on foot,
verses.second: and there we rejoiced in him.

verses.first: In his might he rules for ever; his eyes keep watch over the nations;
verses.second: let no rebel rise up against him.

verses.first: Bless our God, you peoples;
verses.second: make the voice of his praise to be heard;

verses.first: Who holds our souls in life,
verses.second: and will not allow our feet to slip.

verses.first: For you, O God, have proved us;
verses.second: you have tried us just as silver is tried.

verses.first: You brought us into the snare;
verses.second: you laid heavy burdens upon our backs.

verses.first: You let enemies ride over our heads; we went through fire and water;
verses.second: but you brought us out into a place of refreshment.

verses.first: I will enter your house with burnt-offerings and will pay you my vows,
verses.second: which I promised with my lips and spoke with my mouth when I was in trouble.

verses.first: I will offer you sacrifices of fat beasts with the smoke of rams;
verses.second: I will give you oxen and goats.

verses.first: Come and listen, all you who fear God,
verses.second: and I will tell you what he has done for me.

verses.first: I called out to him with my mouth,
verses.second: and his praise was on my tongue.

verses.first: If I had found evil in my heart,
verses.second: the Lord would not have heard me;

verses.first: But in truth God has heard me;
verses.second: he has attended to the voice of my prayer.

verses.first: Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer,
verses.second: nor withheld his love from me.

verses.first: May God be merciful to us and bless us,
verses.second: show us the light of his countenance and come to us.

verses.first: Let your ways be known upon earth,
verses.second: your saving health among all nations.

verses.first: Let the peoples praise you, O God;
verses.second: let all the peoples praise you.

verses.first: Let the nations be glad and sing for joy,
verses.second: for you judge the peoples with equity and guide all the nations upon earth.

verses.first: Let the peoples praise you, O God;
verses.second: let all the peoples praise you.

verses.first: The earth has brought forth her increase;
verses.second: may God, our own God, give us his blessing.

verses.first: May God give us his blessing,
verses.second: and may all the ends of the earth stand in awe of him.

verses.first: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered;
verses.second: let those who hate him flee before him.

verses.first: Let them vanish like smoke when the wind drives it away;
verses.second: as the wax melts at the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

verses.first: But let the righteous be glad and rejoice before God;
verses.second: let them also be merry and joyful.

verses.first: Sing to God, sing praises to his Name; exalt him who rides upon the heavens;
verses.second: Yahweh is his Name, rejoice before him!

verses.first: Father of orphans, defender of widows,
verses.second: God in his holy habitation!

verses.first: God gives the solitary a home and brings forth prisoners into freedom;
verses.second: but the rebels shall live in dry places.

verses.first: O God, when you went forth before your people,
verses.second: when you marched through the wilderness,

verses.first: The earth shook, and the skies poured down rain, at the presence of God, the God of Sinai,
verses.second: at the presence of God, the God of Israel.

verses.first: You sent a gracious rain, O God, upon your inheritance;
verses.second: you refreshed the land when it was weary.

verses.first: Your people found their home in it;
verses.second: in your goodness, O God, you have made provision for the poor.

verses.first: The Lord gave the word;
verses.second: great was the company of women who bore the tidings:

verses.first: “Kings with their armies are fleeing away;
verses.second: the women at home are dividing the spoils.”

verses.first: Though you lingered among the sheepfolds,
verses.second: you shall be like a dove whose wings are covered with silver, whose feathers are like green gold.

verses.first: When the Almighty scattered kings,
verses.second: it was like snow falling in Zalmon.

verses.first: O mighty mountain, O hill of Bashan!
verses.second: O rugged mountain, O hill of Bashan!

verses.first: Why do you look with envy, O rugged mountain, at the hill which God chose for his resting place?
verses.second: truly, the Lord will dwell there for ever.

verses.first: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of thousands;
verses.second: the Lord comes in holiness from Sinai.

verses.first: You have gone up on high and led captivity captive; you have received gifts even from your enemies,
verses.second: that the Lord God might dwell among them.

verses.first: Blessed be the Lord day by day,
verses.second: the God of our salvation, who bears our burdens.

verses.first: He is our God, the God of our salvation;
verses.second: God is the Lord, by whom we escape death.

verses.first: God shall crush the heads of his enemies,
verses.second: and the hairy scalp of those who go on still in their wickedness.

verses.first: The Lord has said, “I will bring them back from Bashan;
verses.second: I will bring them back from the depths of the sea;

verses.first: That your foot may be dipped in blood,
verses.second: the tongues of your dogs in the blood of your enemies.”

verses.first: They see your procession, O God,
verses.second: your procession into the sanctuary, my God and my King.

verses.first: The singers go before, musicians follow after,
verses.second: in the midst of maidens playing upon the hand-drums.

verses.first: Bless God in the congregation;
verses.second: bless the Lord, you that are of the fountain of Israel.

verses.first: There is Benjamin, least of the tribes, at the head; the princes of Judah in a company;
verses.second: and the princes of Zebulon and Naphtali.

verses.first: Send forth your strength, O God;
verses.second: establish, O God, what you have wrought for us.

verses.first: Kings shall bring gifts to you,
verses.second: for your temple’s sake at Jerusalem.

verses.first: Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds,
verses.second: and the peoples, a herd of wild bulls with its calves.

verses.first: Trample down those who lust after silver;
verses.second: scatter the peoples that delight in war.

verses.first: Let tribute be brought out of Egypt;
verses.second: let Ethiopia stretch out her hands to God.

verses.first: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth;
verses.second: sing praises to the Lord.

verses.first: He rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens;
verses.second: he sends forth his voice, his mighty voice.

verses.first: Ascribe power to God;
verses.second: his majesty is over Israel; his strength is in the skies.

verses.first: How wonderful is God in his holy places!
verses.second: the God of Israel giving strength and power to his people! Blessed be God!

verses.first: Save me, O God,
verses.second: for the waters have risen up to my neck.

verses.first: I am sinking in deep mire,
verses.second: and there is no firm ground for my feet.

verses.first: I have come into deep waters,
verses.second: and the torrent washes over me.

verses.first: I have grown weary with my crying; my throat is inflamed;
verses.second: my eyes have failed from looking for my God.

verses.first: Those who hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head; my lying foes who would destroy me are mighty.
verses.second: Must I then give back what I never stole?

verses.first: O God, you know my foolishness,
verses.second: and my faults are not hidden from you.

verses.first: Let not those who hope in you be put to shame through me, Lord God of hosts;
verses.second: let not those who seek you be disgraced because of me, O God of Israel.

verses.first: Surely, for your sake have I suffered reproach,
verses.second: and shame has covered my face.

verses.first: I have become a stranger to my own kindred,
verses.second: an alien to my mother’s children.

verses.first: Zeal for your house has eaten me up;
verses.second: the scorn of those who scorn you has fallen upon me.

verses.first: I humbled myself with fasting,
verses.second: but that was turned to my reproach.

verses.first: I put on sack-cloth also,
verses.second: and became a byword among them.

verses.first: Those who sit at the gate murmur against me,
verses.second: and the drunkards make songs about me.

verses.first: But as for me, this is my prayer to you,
verses.second: at the time you have set, O Lord:

verses.first: “In your great mercy, O God,
verses.second: answer me with your unfailing help.

verses.first: Save me from the mire; do not let me sink;
verses.second: let me be rescued from those who hate me and out of the deep waters.

verses.first: Let not the torrent of waters wash over me, neither let the deep swallow me up;
verses.second: do not let the Pit shut its mouth upon me.

verses.first: Answer me, O Lord, for your love is kind;
verses.second: in your great compassion, turn to me.’

verses.first: “Hide not your face from your servant;
verses.second: be swift and answer me, for I am in distress.

verses.first: Draw near to me and redeem me;
verses.second: because of my enemies deliver me.

verses.first: You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor;
verses.second: my adversaries are all in your sight.”

verses.first: Reproach has broken my heart, and it cannot be healed;
verses.second: I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I could find no one.

verses.first: They gave me gall to eat,
verses.second: and when I was thirsty, they gave me vinegar to drink.

verses.first: Let the table before them be a trap
verses.second: and their sacred feasts a snare.

verses.first: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see,
verses.second: and give them continual trembling in their loins.

verses.first: Pour out your indignation upon them,
verses.second: and let the fierceness of your anger overtake them.

verses.first: Let their camp be desolate,
verses.second: and let there be none to dwell in their tents.

verses.first: For they persecute him whom you have stricken
verses.second: and add to the pain of those whom you have pierced.

verses.first: Lay to their charge guilt upon guilt,
verses.second: and let them not receive your vindication.

verses.first: Let them be wiped out of the book of the living
verses.second: and not be written among the righteous.

verses.first: As for me, I am afflicted and in pain;
verses.second: your help, O God, will lift me up on high.

verses.first: I will praise the Name of God in song;
verses.second: I will proclaim his greatness with thanksgiving.

verses.first: This will please the Lord more than an offering of oxen,
verses.second: more than bullocks with horns and hoofs.

verses.first: The afflicted shall see and be glad;
verses.second: you who seek God, your heart shall live.

verses.first: For the Lord listens to the needy,
verses.second: and his prisoners he does not despise.

verses.first: Let the heavens and the earth praise him,
verses.second: the seas and all that moves in them;

verses.first: For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah;
verses.second: they shall live there and have it in possession.

verses.first: The children of his servants will inherit it,
verses.second: and those who love his Name will dwell therein.

verses.first: Be pleased, O God, to deliver me;
verses.second: O Lord, make haste to help me.

verses.first: Let those who seek my life be ashamed and altogether dismayed;
verses.second: let those who take pleasure in my misfortune draw back and be disgraced.

verses.first: Let those who say to me “Aha!” and gloat over me turn back,
verses.second: because they are ashamed.

verses.first: Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you;
verses.second: let those who love your salvation say for ever, “Great is the Lord!”

verses.first: But as for me, I am poor and needy;
verses.second: come to me speedily, O God.

verses.first: You are my helper and my deliverer;
verses.second: O Lord, do not tarry.

verses.first: In you, O Lord, have I taken refuge;
verses.second: let me never be ashamed.

verses.first: In your righteousness, deliver me and set me free;
verses.second: incline your ear to me and save me.

verses.first: Be my strong rock, a castle to keep me safe;
verses.second: you are my crag and my stronghold.

verses.first: Deliver me, my God, from the hand of the wicked,
verses.second: from the clutches of the evildoer and the oppressor.

verses.first: For you are my hope, O Lord God,
verses.second: my confidence since I was young.

verses.first: I have been sustained by you ever since I was born; from my mother’s womb you have been my strength;
verses.second: my praise shall be always of you.

verses.first: I have become a portent to many;
verses.second: but you are my refuge and my strength.

verses.first: Let my mouth be full of your praise
verses.second: and your glory all the day long.

verses.first: Do not cast me off in my old age;
verses.second: forsake me not when my strength fails.

verses.first: For my enemies are talking against me,
verses.second: and those who lie in wait for my life take counsel together.

verses.first: They say, “God has forsaken him; go after him and seize him;
verses.second: because there is none who will save.”

verses.first: O God, be not far from me;
verses.second: come quickly to help me, O my God.

verses.first: Let those who set themselves against me be put to shame and be disgraced;
verses.second: let those who seek to do me evil be covered with scorn and reproach.

verses.first: But I shall always wait in patience,
verses.second: and shall praise you more and more.

verses.first: My mouth shall recount your mighty acts and saving deeds all day long;
verses.second: though I cannot know the number of them.

verses.first: I will begin with the mighty works of the Lord God
verses.second: I will recall your righteousness, yours alone.

verses.first: O God, you have taught me since I was young,
verses.second: and to this day I tell of your wonderful works.

verses.first: And now that I am old and gray-headed, O God, do not forsake me,
verses.second: till I make known your strength to this generation and your power to all who are to come.

verses.first: Your righteousness, O God, reaches to the heavens;
verses.second: you have done great things; who is like you, O God?

verses.first: You have showed me great troubles and adversities,
verses.second: but you will restore my life and bring me up again from the deep places of the earth.

verses.first: You strengthen me more and more;
verses.second: you enfold and comfort me,

verses.first: Therefore I will praise you upon the lyre for your faithfulness, O my God;
verses.second: I will sing to you with the harp, O Holy One of Israel.

verses.first: My lips will sing with joy when I play to you,
verses.second: and so will my soul, which you have redeemed.

verses.first: My tongue will proclaim your righteousness all day long,
verses.second: for they are ashamed and disgraced who sought to do me harm.

verses.first: Give the King your justice, O God,
verses.second: and your righteousness to the King’s Son;

verses.first: That he may rule your people righteously
verses.second: and the poor with justice;

verses.first: That the mountains may bring prosperity to the people,
verses.second: and the little hills bring righteousness.

verses.first: He shall defend the needy among the people;
verses.second: he shall rescue the poor and crush the oppressor.

verses.first: He shall live as long as the sun and moon endure,
verses.second: from one generation to another.

verses.first: He shall come down like rain upon the mown field,
verses.second: like showers that water the earth.

verses.first: In his time shall the righteous flourish;
verses.second: there shall be abundance of peace till the moon shall be no more.

verses.first: He shall rule from sea to sea,
verses.second: and from the River to the ends of the earth.

verses.first: His foes shall bow down before him,
verses.second: and his enemies lick the dust.

verses.first: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall pay tribute,
verses.second: and the kings of Arabia and Saba offer gifts.

verses.first: All kings shall bow down before him,
verses.second: and all the nations do him service.

verses.first: For he shall deliver the poor who cries out in distress,
verses.second: and the oppressed who has no helper.

verses.first: He shall have pity on the lowly and poor;
verses.second: he shall preserve the lives of the needy.

verses.first: He shall redeem their lives from oppression and violence,
verses.second: and dear shall their blood be in his sight.

verses.first: Long may he live! and may there be given to him gold from Arabia;
verses.second: may prayer be made for him always, and may they bless him all the day long.

verses.first: May there be abundance of grain on the earth, growing thick even on the hilltops;
verses.second: may its fruit flourish like Lebanon, and its grain like grass upon the earth.

verses.first: May his Name remain for ever and be established as long as the sun endures;
verses.second: may all the nations bless themselves in him and call him blessed.

verses.first: Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel,
verses.second: who alone does wondrous deeds!

verses.first: And blessed be his glorious Name for ever!
verses.second: and may all the earth be filled with his glory. Amen. Amen. Book Three

verses.first: Truly, God is good to Israel,
verses.second: to those who are pure in heart.

verses.first: But as for me, my feet had nearly slipped;
verses.second: I had almost tripped and fallen;

verses.first: Because I envied the proud
verses.second: and saw the prosperity of the wicked:

verses.first: For they suffer no pain,
verses.second: and their bodies are sleek and sound;

verses.first: In the misfortunes of others they have no share;
verses.second: they are not afflicted as others are;

verses.first: Therefore they wear their pride like a necklace
verses.second: and wrap their violence about them like a cloak.

verses.first: Their iniquity comes from gross minds,
verses.second: and their hearts overflow with wicked thoughts.

verses.first: They scoff and speak maliciously;
verses.second: out of their haughtiness they plan oppression.

verses.first: They set their mouths against the heavens,
verses.second: and their evil speech runs through the world.

verses.first: And so the people turn to them
verses.second: and find in them no fault.

verses.first: They say, “How should God know?
verses.second: is there knowledge in the Most High?”

verses.first: So then, these are the wicked;
verses.second: always at ease, they increase their wealth.

verses.first: In vain have I kept my heart clean,
verses.second: and washed my hands in innocence.

verses.first: I have been afflicted all day long,
verses.second: and punished every morning.

verses.first: Had I gone on speaking this way,
verses.second: I should have betrayed the generation of your children.

verses.first: When I tried to understand these things,
verses.second: it was too hard for me;

verses.first: Until I entered the sanctuary of God
verses.second: and discerned the end of the wicked.

verses.first: Surely, you set them in slippery places;
verses.second: you cast them down in ruin.

verses.first: Oh, how suddenly do they come to destruction,
verses.second: come to an end, and perish from terror!

verses.first: Like a dream when one awakens, O Lord,
verses.second: when you arise you will make their image vanish.

verses.first: When my mind became embittered,
verses.second: I was sorely wounded in my heart.

verses.first: I was stupid and had no understanding;
verses.second: I was like a brute beast in your presence.

verses.first: Yet I am always with you;
verses.second: you hold me by my right hand.

verses.first: You will guide me by your counsel,
verses.second: and afterwards receive me with glory.

verses.first: Whom have I in heaven but you?
verses.second: and having you I desire nothing upon earth.

verses.first: Though my flesh and my heart should waste away,
verses.second: God is the strength of my heart and my portion for ever.

verses.first: Truly, those who forsake you will perish;
verses.second: you destroy all who are unfaithful.

verses.first: But it is good for me to be near God;
verses.second: I have made the Lord God my refuge.

verses.first: I will speak of all your works
verses.second: in the gates of the city of Zion.

verses.first: O God, why have you utterly cast us off?
verses.second: why is your wrath so hot against the sheep of your pasture?

verses.first: Remember your congregation that you purchased long ago,
verses.second: the tribe you redeemed to be your inheritance, and Mount Zion where you dwell.

verses.first: Turn your steps toward the endless ruins;
verses.second: the enemy has laid waste everything in your sanctuary.

verses.first: Your adversaries roared in your holy place;
verses.second: they set up their banners as tokens of victory.

verses.first: They were like men coming up with axes to a grove of trees;
verses.second: they broke down all your carved work with hatchets and hammers.

verses.first: They set fire to your holy place;
verses.second: they defiled the dwelling-place of your Name and razed it to the ground.

verses.first: They said to themselves, “Let us destroy them altogether.”
verses.second: They burned down all the meeting-places of God in the land.

verses.first: There are no signs for us to see; there is no prophet left;
verses.second: there is not one among us who knows how long.

verses.first: How long, O God, will the adversary scoff?
verses.second: will the enemy blaspheme your Name for ever?

verses.first: Why do you draw back your hand?
verses.second: why is your right hand hidden in your bosom?

verses.first: Yet God is my King from ancient times,
verses.second: victorious in the midst of the earth.

verses.first: You divided the sea by your might
verses.second: and shattered the heads of the dragons upon the waters;

verses.first: You crushed the heads of Leviathan
verses.second: and gave him to the people of the desert for food.

verses.first: You split open spring and torrent;
verses.second: you dried up ever-flowing rivers.

verses.first: Yours is the day, yours also the night;
verses.second: you established the moon and the sun.

verses.first: You fixed all the boundaries of the earth;
verses.second: you made both summer and winter.

verses.first: Remember, O Lord, how the enemy scoffed,
verses.second: how a foolish people despised your Name.

verses.first: Do not hand over the life of your dove to wild beasts;
verses.second: never forget the lives of your poor.

verses.first: Look upon your covenant;
verses.second: the dark places of the earth are haunts of violence.

verses.first: Let not the oppressed turn away ashamed;
verses.second: let the poor and needy praise your Name.

verses.first: Arise, O God, maintain your cause;
verses.second: remember how fools revile you all day long.

verses.first: Forget not the clamor of your adversaries,
verses.second: the unending tumult of those who rise up against you.

verses.first: We give you thanks, O God, we give you thanks,
verses.second: calling upon your Name and declaring all your wonderful deeds.

verses.first: “I will appoint a time,” says God;
verses.second: “I will judge with equity.

verses.first: Though the earth and all its inhabitants are quaking,
verses.second: I will make its pillars fast.

verses.first: I will say to the boasters, ‘Boast no more,’
verses.second: and to the wicked, ‘Do not toss your horns;

verses.first: Do not toss your horns so high,
verses.second: nor speak with a proud neck.’”

verses.first: For judgment is neither from the east nor from the west,
verses.second: nor yet from the wilderness or the mountains.

verses.first: It is God who judges;
verses.second: he puts down one and lifts up another.

verses.first: For in the Lord’s hand there is a cup, full of spiced and foaming wine, which he pours out,
verses.second: and all the wicked of the earth shall drink and drain the dregs.

verses.first: But I will rejoice for ever;
verses.second: I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.

verses.first: He shall break off all the horns of the wicked;
verses.second: but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.
